analysis:
Source pass over base_text units of provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/KVCacheSSD/SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift (base lines 3039-4237). The base side has no changed ranges. Head range 3140-3240 inserts new tests after the malformedLookalikePreserved test (base 3117-3138). The patch excerpt shows two of them:
- remembersHeaderVerdictsOnlyForUnchangedFiles: a header corrupted after an earlier pass, with size and mtime restored, must lose its DBK3 ownership proof (filesSeen==0, no TTL or budget eviction).
- replacedLookalikeIsReadAgain: a malformed lookalike later replaced by a real block becomes owned on the next pass.

This implies SSDWholeRootMaintainer now caches header-ownership verdicts, keyed on file identity (likely inode, size, mtime and ctime). Those sources are not supplied.

Security relevance (T-041 cleanup and TTL purge semantics; TB-003 operator vs process; T-016 disk DoS):
- A stale cached verdict could let the maintainer delete a non-owned file (data-loss tampering).
- Conversely, it could keep an expired owned file past the TTL, extending at-rest retention beyond the 30-minute bound.

The tests assert fail-closed preservation and re-reading on replacement, which matches the intended ownership model. Test-only changes introduce no runtime attack surface.

Integration must verify in SSDWholeRootMaintainer (production source, not supplied):
- The verdict-cache key includes ctime/inode so content changes invalidate it.
- Cache entries are bounded so many lookalikes cannot grow memory without limit.
- A cached 'owned' verdict cannot survive replacement of the file by a non-DBK3 file or a symlink; the existing symlinked-root rejection test is at base 3140-3172.
- Positive verdicts are not reused after a file is swapped with a same-size, same-mtime file.

Remaining base content covers:
- Donation gate, write-behind bounds and outcome recording.
- Windowed sidecar tests: HMAC domain separation and keyed windowBase commitment in the AAD, with no raw position (base 3925-3982).

These are unchanged and consistent with T-041(a)/(c).
